title: EditOp
description: One edit op on a timeline (timeline spec v1), told apart by its "op" field. The editor agent changes a timeline only by sending a batch of these ops (the opBatch definition). A batch is atomic: every op is applied in order to a copy, the main track is rippled so it stays contiguous, new ids are assigned, and the result is validated. If anything is wrong, nothing changes and every problem is reported with the index of the op that caused it. All times are integer milliseconds.
$comment: Structure only. The Go package apps/server/internal/timeline/ops applies the ops and checks what a schema cannot: that ids exist and are of the right kind, that a clip index is in range, that the result is a valid timeline (docs/design/timeline-v1.md sections 3 and 4). The shared definitions (ms, itemId, assetId, reframe, transition, ...) are copies of the ones in v1.schema.json; a test keeps them equal. The schema is closed: no property is allowed outside the ones listed.

ms.title: Milliseconds
ms.description: A time or duration as a whole number of milliseconds, from 0 to 86 400 000 (24 hours). No floats.

gainDb.title: Gain in dB
gainDb.description: Volume change in decibels, from -30 to +6. 0 leaves the level as it is.

itemId.title: Item id
itemId.description: A lowercase id of 1 to 32 characters: a letter, then letters, digits or underscores, such as "c1" or "t3". Ids are unique across the whole spec. The edit ops name items by these ids.

styleId.title: Style id
styleId.description: The id of a text style from the style registry, such as "title_bold". The spec can't name a font directly.

assetId.title: Asset id
assetId.description: TypeID of an asset: the prefix "ast_" and a 26-character base32 UUIDv7.

momentId.title: Moment id
momentId.description: TypeID of a moment: the prefix "mom_" and a 26-character base32 UUIDv7.

trendId.title: Trend id
trendId.description: TypeID of a trend: the prefix "trd_" and a 26-character base32 UUIDv7.

licenseId.title: Licence id
licenseId.description: TypeID of a licence: the prefix "lic_" and a 26-character base32 UUIDv7.

reframe.title: Reframe
reframe.description: How the source is fitted to the output frame. Without it, the clip uses cover, focus 0.5/0.5 and zoom 1.

mode.title: Mode
mode.description: cover fills the frame and crops around the focus point. contain fits the whole source and pads with the background colour. blur_fill fits the whole source over a blurred, scaled copy of itself.

focus.title: Focus point
focus.description: The point of the source that the crop is centred on, as fractions of its width and height. Default 0.5/0.5. Only cover uses it.

x.title: Focus x
x.description: 0 is the left edge of the source, 1 the right edge.

y.title: Focus y
y.description: 0 is the top edge of the source, 1 the bottom edge.

zoom.title: Zoom
zoom.description: Extra zoom into the centre of the framed clip, from 1 (none) to 3. Default 1.

look.title: Look
look.description: A colour treatment for the clip. Without it, the clip has no treatment.

preset.title: Preset
preset.description: A fixed colour preset: none, punchy (more contrast and saturation), warm, cool, bw (black and white), matte (lifted blacks), auto (a mild contrast curve that keeps blacks and whites where they are, plus the clip's exposure_ev nudge, so shots from different angles meet at one exposure without washing out low-key footage) or gym_moody (warm skin, a little contrast above the shadows, a soft vignette; dark shadows are left alone).

match.title: Match exposure
match.description: True to correct the clip's exposure by its exposure_ev hint (from the analysis; a nudge of at most 0.7 stops, black point kept) before the preset, so shots from different angles meet at one exposure. The preset auto always does this, whatever match says. Default false. Without an exposure_ev on the clip it changes nothing.

transition.title: Transition in
transition.description: How the clip begins. A cut is instant. The other types blend with the previous clip over duration_ms, and the clip then starts that long before the previous one ends. The first clip must have a cut.

type.title: Type
type.description: crossfade blends the two clips. dip_to_black fades out to black and in again. whip_left is a fast slide to the left with motion blur (whip is the same, kept for older edits); whip_right slides to the right. zoom_through zooms into the outgoing clip and out of the incoming one through a blur. flash dips to white.

duration_ms.title: Duration
duration_ms.description: Length of the transition in ms, 100 to 1000. It must be shorter than both clips it joins (checked by the Go layer).

videoAudio.title: Clip audio
videoAudio.description: What the clip's own sound does: mode mute, bed or full (or the old use_source). Without it, the clip is silent.

mode.title: Mode
mode.description: What the clip's own sound does. mute: nothing (the default: a clip with no audio settings is silent). bed: a low ambience under the edit, evened out across the clips and never normalised up to the programme, so the export is not silent where no sound is playing and the creator can add a trend sound on top; use it for footage with no speech (gym clatter, room tone). full: the programme: the clip's sound at its own level, normalised with the rest and ducked under sound effects; use it for speech. gain_db is a trim on top of the mode's level.

use_source.title: Use source audio
use_source.description: The old spelling of mode: true is full, false is mute. Not together with mode.

gain_db.title: Gain
gain_db.description: Volume change of the clip's audio in dB, from -30 to +6. Default 0.

audioDuration.title: Duration
audioDuration.description: How long the sound plays, in ms, 1 or more. Without it, it plays to the end of the timeline. The sound must end inside the total duration, and source_offset_ms + this duration must fit inside the asset (both checked by the Go layer).

fadeIn.title: Fade in
fadeIn.description: Length of the fade in at the start, in ms. Without it, there is no fade. fade_in_ms + fade_out_ms must not exceed the sound's duration (checked by the Go layer).

fadeOut.title: Fade out
fadeOut.description: Length of the fade out at the end, in ms. Without it, there is no fade. fade_in_ms + fade_out_ms must not exceed the sound's duration (checked by the Go layer).

speed.title: Speed
speed.description: Playback speed from 0.25 (slow motion) to 4 (fast). Default 1. A clip has either speed or speed_ramp, not both (checked by the Go layer).

sourceRange.title: Source range
sourceRange.description: The part of the asset to use, in the asset's own time. in_ms must be below out_ms and out_ms within the asset's duration (checked by the Go layer).

in_ms.title: In point
in_ms.description: Where the clip starts in the asset, in ms.

out_ms.title: Out point
out_ms.description: Where the clip ends in the asset, in ms. Exclusive.

why.title: Why
why.description: Why the editor picked this clip, 280 characters at most. Shown to the creator in the UI and never rendered.

textBody.title: Text
textBody.description: The words to show: 1 to 120 characters and at most 3 lines. Lines are separated by a newline (\n). No other control character is allowed, and neither are the line and paragraph separators U+2028 and U+2029.

textFill.title: Fill colour
textFill.description: The colour of the letters as #RRGGBB, for this text only (for example #F2E9A0). Without it the style's own colour is used.

textScale.title: Size scale
textScale.description: The size of the text relative to its style's size, from 0.6 to 1.4 (kept to a hundredth). Without it the style's own size (1) is used.

textShadow.title: Shadow
textShadow.description: The drop shadow of the letters: none, soft (a light one) or strong (a heavy one). Without it the style's own shadow is used.

textAlign.title: Alignment
textAlign.description: How the lines of a text of more than one line sit against each other in its box: left, center or right. Default center.

textAvoidSubject.title: Avoid the subject
textAvoidSubject.description: Whether the renderer keeps this text off the head of the person in the footage: when it would cover the head it is moved above or below it inside the safe zone, or shrunk within the allowed scale. true by default; set false to place the text exactly where its anchor or position puts it.

textAnimation.title: Animation
textAnimation.description: How the text enters: none, pop_in, fade, typewriter or slide_up. Default none.

textAnchor.title: Anchor
textAnchor.description: A safe place for the text: upper_third, center or lower_third. Set this or position, not both.

textPosition.title: Position
textPosition.description: A free place for the text's centre as fractions of the frame. The text must stay inside the format's safe zone (checked by the Go layer). Set this or anchor, not both.

x.title: Position x
x.description: 0 is the left edge of the frame, 1 the right edge.

y.title: Position y
y.description: 0 is the top edge of the frame, 1 the bottom edge.

textDuration.title: Duration
textDuration.description: How long the text stays, in ms. At least 300. It must end inside the total duration (checked by the Go layer).

captionsStyle.title: Style
captionsStyle.description: word_highlight shows a few words and highlights the one being said. chunk shows each group of words at once.

maxWords.title: Maximum words
maxWords.description: The most words on screen at once, 1 to 4. Default 2.

add_clip.title: add_clip
add_clip.description: Add a clip from a source asset to the main track. Give the part of the asset to use as source.in_ms and source.out_ms (in the asset's own time; in_ms below out_ms, out_ms within the asset's duration). Say where it goes with index (the position it will have, 0 is the start) or after_id (right after that clip); without either it goes at the end. The clips after it move later (ripple) and their at_ms is recomputed. Without id, the clip gets the next free id such as "c7"; the result reports it. speed (or speed_ramp), reframe, motion, look, transition_in and audio are optional and default as in the timeline spec. A transition_in on a clip that ends up first is an error.

id.title: Clip id
id.description: Optional id for the new clip. Without it the next free "c<n>" is used. It must not be in use anywhere in the timeline.

index.title: Index
index.description: The position the new clip will have among the main clips, 0 for the start. Equal to the number of clips appends. Not together with after_id.

after_id.title: After
after_id.description: Put the new clip right after the clip with this id. Not together with index.

remove_item.title: remove_item
remove_item.description: Remove a clip from the main track. The clips after it move earlier (ripple). If the removed clip was first, the new first clip loses its transition_in (it becomes a cut). Text and sounds keep their times, so one that now runs past the end of the timeline is an error: shorten or move it in the same batch.

id.title: Clip id
id.description: The id of the main-track clip to remove.

move_item.title: move_item
move_item.description: Move an item. For a main-track clip, give index (the position it will have, 0 is the start) or after_id (right after that clip); the clips between shift and every at_ms is recomputed. For a text item or a sound, give at_ms, its new absolute start; nothing else moves. Give exactly one of at_ms, index and after_id. A clip that moves to the first position loses its transition_in.

id.title: Item id
id.description: The id of the clip, text item or sound to move.

at_ms.title: Start
at_ms.description: New start in ms. Only for a text item or a sound.

index.title: Index
index.description: The position the clip will have among the main clips, 0 for the start. Only for a clip.

after_id.title: After
after_id.description: Put the clip right after the clip with this id. Only for a clip.

trim_item.title: trim_item
trim_item.description: Trim an item. For a main-track clip, give in_ms and/or out_ms: the new source range in the asset's own time (absolute values, not changes). The clip's length changes and the clips after it ripple. For a text item or a sound, give duration_ms, its new length; it starts where it did. Do not mix the two kinds of fields.

id.title: Item id
id.description: The id of the clip, text item or sound to trim.

in_ms.title: In point
in_ms.description: New source in point of a clip, in ms. Must stay below the out point.

out_ms.title: Out point
out_ms.description: New source out point of a clip, in ms. Must stay within the asset's duration.

duration_ms.title: Duration
duration_ms.description: New length of a text item (at least 300) or a sound (at least 1), in ms.

replace_source.title: replace_source
replace_source.description: Swap the asset and source range of a clip and keep everything else about it: its place, speed, reframe, look, transition and audio settings. The clips after it ripple if the new range has another length. The clip's moment_id is replaced by the given one, or removed when you give none, because the old moment no longer matches.

id.title: Clip id
id.description: The id of the main-track clip to change.

set_speed.title: set_speed
set_speed.description: Set the playback speed of a clip, from 0.25 (slow motion) to 4 (fast). A faster speed makes the clip shorter and the clips after it ripple earlier. It also removes a speed_ramp the clip had, since the ramp replaces the speed.

id.title: Clip id
id.description: The id of the main-track clip.

set_reframe.title: set_reframe
set_reframe.description: Set how a clip is fitted to the output frame: cover (fill and crop around focus), contain (fit and pad) or blur_fill (fit over a blurred copy). This replaces the whole reframe of the clip, so fields you leave out go back to their defaults (focus 0.5/0.5, zoom 1).

id.title: Clip id
id.description: The id of the main-track clip.

mode.title: Mode
mode.description: cover fills the frame and crops around the focus point. contain fits the whole source and pads with the background colour. blur_fill fits the whole source over a blurred, scaled copy of itself.

focus.title: Focus point
focus.description: The point of the source that the crop is centred on, as fractions of its width and height. Default 0.5/0.5. Only cover uses it.

x.title: Focus x
x.description: 0 is the left edge of the source, 1 the right edge.

y.title: Focus y
y.description: 0 is the top edge of the source, 1 the bottom edge.

zoom.title: Zoom
zoom.description: Extra zoom into the centre of the framed clip, from 1 (none) to 3. Default 1.

add_text.title: add_text
add_text.description: Add a text overlay. It keeps its absolute time when clips move, and it must end inside the total duration of the timeline and inside the safe zone of the format. Give exactly one of anchor and position. Without id, the text gets the next free id such as "t3"; the result reports it. The text track is created when there is none.

id.title: Text id
id.description: Optional id for the new text item. Without it the next free "t<n>" is used.

at_ms.title: Start
at_ms.description: When the text appears, in ms.

update_text.title: update_text
update_text.description: Change fields of a text item; the fields you leave out stay as they are, except that changing the style resets fill, scale, shadow and align to the new style's own: restate the ones you want to keep. Setting anchor removes the position and the other way round. Give at least one field.

id.title: Text id
id.description: The id of the text item.

id.title: Text id
id.description: The id of the text item to remove.

set_transition.title: set_transition
set_transition.description: Set how a clip begins. cut is instant. crossfade, dip_to_black, whip_left (whip is the same), whip_right, zoom_through and flash blend with the previous clip over duration_ms (100 to 1000) and the clip then starts that long before the previous one ends, so the clips after it ripple earlier. whip_left and whip_right are fast slides with motion blur, zoom_through zooms into the outgoing clip and out of the incoming one, flash dips to white. The first clip must have a cut, and a transition must be shorter than both clips it joins.

id.title: Clip id
id.description: The id of the main-track clip whose start gets the transition.

type.title: Type
type.description: cut, crossfade, dip_to_black, whip (same as whip_left), whip_left, whip_right, zoom_through or flash.

duration_ms.title: Duration
duration_ms.description: Length of the transition in ms, 100 to 1000. It must be shorter than both clips it joins (checked by the Go layer).

set_sound.title: set_sound
set_sound.description: Add a sound, or replace the sound with the same id (a full replacement: fields you leave out go back to their defaults). export is set for you from the kind: a trend_sound is cue_only (a cue for the creator to add the sound in TikTok; we never reproduce it), the other two are licensed. Sounds keep their absolute time when clips move, must end inside the total duration, and the audio track is created when there is none. A licensed_track needs an audio asset with a licence, a creator_audio an audio asset with a rights attestation.

oneOf.title: set_sound trend_sound
oneOf.description: Add a sound, or replace the sound with the same id (a full replacement: fields you leave out go back to their defaults). export is set for you from the kind: a trend_sound is cue_only (a cue for the creator to add the sound in TikTok; we never reproduce it), the other two are licensed. Sounds keep their absolute time when clips move, must end inside the total duration, and the audio track is created when there is none. A licensed_track needs an audio asset with a licence, a creator_audio an audio asset with a rights attestation. This variant: trend_sound.

id.title: Sound id
id.description: Optional id. If a sound with this id exists, it is replaced entirely; if not, a new sound gets this id. Without id, a new sound gets the next free "s<n>".

at_ms.title: Start
at_ms.description: When the sound starts in the output, in ms. Default 0.

source_offset_ms.title: Source offset
source_offset_ms.description: Where in the sound to start playing, in ms. Default 0.

oneOf.title: set_sound licensed_track
oneOf.description: Add a sound, or replace the sound with the same id (a full replacement: fields you leave out go back to their defaults). export is set for you from the kind: a trend_sound is cue_only (a cue for the creator to add the sound in TikTok; we never reproduce it), the other two are licensed. Sounds keep their absolute time when clips move, must end inside the total duration, and the audio track is created when there is none. A licensed_track needs an audio asset with a licence, a creator_audio an audio asset with a rights attestation. This variant: licensed_track.

id.title: Sound id
id.description: Optional id. If a sound with this id exists, it is replaced entirely; if not, a new sound gets this id. Without id, a new sound gets the next free "s<n>".

at_ms.title: Start
at_ms.description: When the sound starts in the output, in ms. Default 0.

source_offset_ms.title: Source offset
source_offset_ms.description: Where in the sound to start playing, in ms. Default 0.

oneOf.title: set_sound creator_audio
oneOf.description: Add a sound, or replace the sound with the same id (a full replacement: fields you leave out go back to their defaults). export is set for you from the kind: a trend_sound is cue_only (a cue for the creator to add the sound in TikTok; we never reproduce it), the other two are licensed. Sounds keep their absolute time when clips move, must end inside the total duration, and the audio track is created when there is none. A licensed_track needs an audio asset with a licence, a creator_audio an audio asset with a rights attestation. This variant: creator_audio.

id.title: Sound id
id.description: Optional id. If a sound with this id exists, it is replaced entirely; if not, a new sound gets this id. Without id, a new sound gets the next free "s<n>".

at_ms.title: Start
at_ms.description: When the sound starts in the output, in ms. Default 0.

source_offset_ms.title: Source offset
source_offset_ms.description: Where in the sound to start playing, in ms. Default 0.

remove_sound.title: remove_sound
remove_sound.description: Remove a sound from the audio track.

id.title: Sound id
id.description: The id of the sound to remove.

beatGrid.title: Beat grid
beatGrid.description: The beats of a sound, in the sound's own time (ms from its start) unless the op says otherwise. Either a constant tempo (bpm and first_beat_ms) or an explicit list of beat times (beats_ms) from beat tracking.

oneOf.title: Constant tempo
oneOf.description: A grid of evenly spaced beats: beat n is at first_beat_ms + n * 60000 / bpm.

first_beat_ms.title: First beat
first_beat_ms.description: Time of the first beat in ms from the start of the sound. May have a fraction.

beats_per_bar.title: Beats per bar
beats_per_bar.description: Beats in a bar, 1 to 16. Default 4.

downbeat_offset.title: Downbeat offset
downbeat_offset.description: Number of beats from the first beat to the first downbeat, less than beats_per_bar. Default 0.

oneOf.title: Beat list
oneOf.description: An explicit list of beat times, possibly irregular.

beats_ms.title: Beats
beats_ms.description: Beat times in ms from the start of the sound: at least two, strictly increasing and at least 250 ms apart.

downbeats_ms.title: Downbeats
downbeats_ms.description: Times of the downbeats; each must coincide with one of the beats. Without it, every beats_per_bar-th beat from the first is a downbeat.

beats_per_bar.title: Beats per bar
beats_per_bar.description: Beats in a bar, 1 to 16. Default 4.

max_shift_ms.title: Maximum shift
max_shift_ms.description: The furthest a cut may move to reach a beat, in ms. When both limits are given the smaller applies; without either it is half a beat.

max_shift_beats.title: Maximum shift in beats
max_shift_beats.description: The furthest a cut may move, in beats.

prefer_downbeats.title: Prefer downbeats
prefer_downbeats.description: Pick the nearest downbeat within the limit when there is one. A cut already on a beat stays there. Default false.

min_shot_ms.title: Minimum shot
min_shot_ms.description: The shortest shot to keep, in ms. Default 300.

write_markers.title: Write markers
write_markers.description: Also replace the beat and downbeat markers of the timeline with this grid's beats. Default false.

snap_cuts_to_beats.title: snap_cuts_to_beats
snap_cuts_to_beats.description: Move the cuts between main-track clips onto the beats of a grid, so the edit cuts on the music. Each cut (the at_ms of every clip after the first) moves to the nearest beat within the maximum shift (half a beat unless set), aligned to a frame, by trimming the end of the clip before it and the start of the clip after it; the total length does not change. A cut with no beat in range, or where moving would make a shot too short (under 300 ms) or run a clip past the end of its asset, stays where it is, and the result says so in a warning. If sound_id names a sound on the audio track, the grid is in that sound's time and is placed with the sound's at_ms and source_offset_ms; without it the grid is in timeline time.

sound_id.title: Sound id
sound_id.description: The id of the sound the grid belongs to. Without it the grid is in timeline time.

set_look.title: set_look
set_look.description: Set the colour look of a clip. Without id it applies to every clip on the main track. Presets: none, punchy, warm, cool, bw, matte, auto (a mild contrast curve that keeps blacks and whites, plus each clip's exposure_ev nudge, so shots from different angles meet at one exposure) and gym_moody (warm skin, a little contrast above the shadows and a soft vignette, with dark shadows left alone: the grade for gym footage). match true also corrects each clip's exposure by its exposure_ev hint (a nudge of at most 0.7 stops, black point kept; auto always does) before the preset (left out, match keeps what the clip had). exposure_ev sets that hint on one clip (it needs id; 0 clears it, and replace_source clears it too); the analysis writes it, so only give it when you know the clip's exposure; it is -1 to 1 and must not come from a clip's mean brightness (low-key footage is dark and correct).

id.title: Clip id
id.description: The id of the main-track clip. Leave it out for all clips.

preset.title: Preset
preset.description: A fixed colour preset: none, punchy (more contrast and saturation), warm, cool, bw (black and white), matte (lifted blacks), auto (a mild contrast curve that keeps blacks and whites where they are, plus the clip's exposure_ev nudge, so shots from different angles meet at one exposure without washing out low-key footage) or gym_moody (warm skin, a little contrast above the shadows, a soft vignette; dark shadows are left alone).

match.title: Match exposure
match.description: True to correct the clip's exposure by its exposure_ev hint (from the analysis; a nudge of at most 0.7 stops, black point kept) before the preset, so shots from different angles meet at one exposure. The preset auto always does this, whatever match says. Default false. Without an exposure_ev on the clip it changes nothing.

set_captions.title: set_captions
set_captions.description: Create or change the captions track (burned-in captions from the transcript). The fields you leave out stay as they are; on a new captions track style defaults to word_highlight and enabled to true. Give at least one field.

uppercase.title: Uppercase
uppercase.description: True to write the captions in capitals. Default true.

set_clip_audio.title: set_clip_audio
set_clip_audio.description: Set what a clip's own sound does and how loud. mode is mute (nothing; the default), bed (a low ambience under the edit, evened out across clips and never normalised up to the programme: for footage with no speech) or full (the programme, for speech). Without id it sets every clip of the main track, which is how to set the bed policy once. The fields you leave out stay as they are. use_source is the old spelling of full and mute; give mode or use_source, not both.

id.title: Clip id
id.description: The id of the main-track clip. Without it every clip of the main track.

mode.title: Mode
mode.description: What the clip's own sound does. mute: nothing (the default: a clip with no audio settings is silent). bed: a low ambience under the edit, evened out across the clips and never normalised up to the programme, so the export is not silent where no sound is playing and the creator can add a trend sound on top; use it for footage with no speech (gym clatter, room tone). full: the programme: the clip's sound at its own level, normalised with the rest and ducked under sound effects; use it for speech. gain_db is a trim on top of the mode's level.

use_source.title: Use source audio
use_source.description: The old spelling of mode: true is full, false is mute. Not together with mode.

gain_db.title: Gain
gain_db.description: Volume change of the clip's audio in dB, from -30 to +6. Default 0.

opBatch.title: EditBatch
opBatch.description: A batch of edit ops, applied in order and atomically: all of them or none. At most 100 ops.

motion.title: Motion
motion.description: A camera move on the clip, applied as a digital zoom on the already-reframed frame (after reframe, so it composes with every reframe mode and never shows a border). punch_in is a fast zoom (about 5 frames) that lands at at_ms and holds, push_in a slow continuous zoom over the whole clip, pull_back the reverse (starts zoomed, pulls back to the full frame), shake a short camera shake that starts at at_ms and dies out (deterministic: the pattern comes from the clip's id), and handheld the living camera of a tripod shot: a slow push over the whole clip, a gentle drift that alternates direction from one clip to the next and a slow sway, so the shot never sits dead still, with a punch-in of 6 % that lands at at_ms when it is given (the drop or a strong beat); the renderer keeps the push off the subject's head and body when the clip has a subject box. Needs a clip of at least 400 ms (checked by the Go layer).

preset.title: Preset
preset.description: none, punch_in, push_in, pull_back, shake or handheld.

at_ms.title: At
at_ms.description: Only for punch_in (where the zoom has landed), shake (where it starts) and handheld (where its punch-in lands): milliseconds from the clip's first frame, inside the clip. Without it punch_in zooms over the first frames of the clip, shake starts at its first frame and handheld has no punch-in.

strength.title: Strength
strength.description: The peak scale increase, 0.05 (5 % bigger) to 0.35. Defaults: punch_in 0.15, push_in 0.1, pull_back 0.15, shake 0.08 (also the size of the shake), handheld 0.08 (the push over the clip).

speedRamp.title: Speed ramp
speedRamp.description: A speed that changes along the clip, as 2 to 16 points {at_ms, speed}. at_ms is a source offset: milliseconds into the clip's source range, counted from source.in_ms (0 to out_ms - in_ms), strictly increasing. The speed (0.25 to 4) changes linearly in source time between two points, is the first point's speed before the first and the last point's speed after the last. The clip's output duration is the integral of 1/speed over its source range. It replaces speed: give one of the two. The clip's own audio is muted (it cannot follow the ramp). Sorted points and the range are checked by the Go layer.

at_ms.title: Source offset
at_ms.description: Where the point is, in ms from source.in_ms (in source time).

speed.title: Speed
speed.description: The playback speed at the point, 0.25 to 4.

set_motion.title: set_motion
set_motion.description: Set the camera move of a clip: a digital zoom or a shake on the already-reframed frame. punch_in is a fast zoom (about 5 frames) that lands at at_ms and holds: use it on a beat. push_in is a slow zoom over the whole clip, pull_back starts zoomed and pulls back to the full frame, shake is a short camera shake that starts at at_ms, and handheld is the living camera of a tripod shot (a slow push, a gentle drift that alternates from clip to clip, a slow sway, and a 6 % punch-in at at_ms when given: put it on the drop or a strong beat). handheld is camera motion, not an effect: give it to every static shot of a creator whose own videos are handheld, so no shot sits dead still. This replaces the clip's whole motion, so fields you leave out go back to their defaults; none removes it. Without id it sets every clip of the main track (no at_ms then): set_motion with preset handheld and no id is the living camera for the whole edit, and a later set_motion with an id changes one clip. The clip must play for at least 400 ms, and at_ms (only for punch_in, shake and handheld) counts from the clip's own first frame, so it stays right when the clip moves.

id.title: Clip id
id.description: The id of the main-track clip. Leave it out to set every clip of the main track.

preset.title: Preset
preset.description: none, punch_in, push_in, pull_back, shake or handheld.

at_ms.title: At
at_ms.description: Only for punch_in (where the zoom has landed), shake (where it starts) and handheld (where its punch-in lands), and only with an id: milliseconds from the clip's first frame, inside the clip. Without it punch_in zooms over the first frames of the clip, shake starts at its first frame and handheld has no punch-in.

strength.title: Strength
strength.description: The peak scale increase, 0.05 (5 % bigger) to 0.35. Defaults: punch_in 0.15, push_in 0.1, pull_back 0.15, shake 0.08 (also the size of the shake), handheld 0.08 (the push over the clip).

set_speed_ramp.title: set_speed_ramp
set_speed_ramp.description: Give a clip a speed that changes along it, for example fast into slow at the peak of a lift: points [{at_ms: 0, speed: 3}, {at_ms: 1500, speed: 3}, {at_ms: 2200, speed: 0.4}]. at_ms is a source offset: milliseconds from the clip's source.in_ms, strictly increasing and within the source range. Between points the speed changes linearly. The clip's length is the integral of the ramp, so it ripples the clips after it. It replaces speed (a set_speed later replaces the ramp), and the clip's own sound in full mode (speech) is muted while it has a ramp; in bed mode it plays at the clip's average speed.

id.title: Clip id
id.description: The id of the main-track clip.

exposureEv.title: Exposure hint
exposureEv.description: A small nudge, -1 to 1 stops (EV): how much brighter this clip is than the exposure the edit should have (positive: too bright, to be darkened; negative: too dark, to be lifted). It must come from highlight or midtone percentiles of the clip, never from its mean brightness, because a low-key clip (black wall, lit subject) has a low mean and is correctly exposed. The renderer applies the opposite, limited to 0.7 stops and ignoring hints under 0.15, with a highlight-preserving curve that keeps the black point, when look.match is true or the preset is auto. Without it, nothing is corrected.

sfxName.title: Effect
sfxName.description: The effect category: whoosh, swish, impact, riser, downlifter, sub_drop, pop, click, glitch, shimmer, sting.

sfxVariant.title: Variant
sfxVariant.description: Optional variant of the effect, one of the variants of its category: whoosh: air, fast, heavy; swish: thin, blade, cloth; impact: punch, deep, crack, metal; riser: tension, sweep, pitch, long; downlifter: fall, short, tape; sub_drop: boom, quick, long; pop: bubble, tick, double; click: ui, soft, tonal, mech; glitch: stutter, crush, chirp; shimmer: sparkle, wash, rise; sting: hit, bright, dark. Without it the category's first variant is used, which is what the effects were before variants existed. "auto" picks one of the category's variants from a hash of the item id, so repeats of one effect differ. Every item also gets a small, deterministic jitter of pitch, length and filter from its id, so two items of the same variant are never exactly the same sample.

add_sfx.title: add_sfx
add_sfx.description: Add a generated sound effect to the audio track (created when there is none). Categories: whoosh (an air pass-by for a whip or a cut; variants air 0.6 s, fast 0.35 s, heavy 1.0 s with weight), swish (a quick thin air pass for small moves; thin 0.3 s, blade 0.2 s, cloth 0.4 s), impact (a low hit with a crack for a punch-in or the drop; punch 0.8 s, deep 1.4 s with a long sub, crack 0.5 s bright, metal 1.2 s), riser (a rising tension build that peaks at its end, so start it that long before the moment it leads to; tension 1.5 s, sweep 1.0 s filter sweep, pitch 2.0 s tonal, long 3.0 s), downlifter (a falling release after a hit or on the new section; fall 1.2 s, short 0.6 s, tape 0.8 s tape stop), sub_drop (a pitch-dropping sine under a hit; boom 1.0 s, quick 0.5 s, long 2.0 s), pop (a small bubble for an element appearing; bubble 0.3 s, tick 0.15 s, double 0.35 s), click (a UI click on the frame of an on-screen press; ui 80 ms, soft 100 ms, tonal 120 ms, mech 180 ms), glitch (a digital stutter for a glitchy cut; stutter 0.3 s, crush 0.25 s, chirp 0.4 s), shimmer (a sparkle for something magical or new; sparkle 1.2 s, wash 1.5 s, rise 1.0 s), sting (a logo or reveal hit with a tonal bloom; hit 2.5 s, bright 2.0 s, dark 3.0 s). Use few: the music and the voice carry most of the edit, effects are accents on the moments that matter (a whoosh on a whip or a cut, an impact or sting on the reveal or the drop, a riser started its length before the moment it leads to, a click on an on-screen press, a pop for an element appearing). A timeline holds about 30 effects at most (more is refused as too_many_effects). The effect is synthesised by us, needs no asset or licence and is always in the render and the export. It starts at at_ms (inside the timeline; it is cut at the end) and is mixed at a level matched to its category plus gain_db, so it stays an accent. With speech (a clip in mode full) it is mixed after the loudness normalisation and the programme is ducked a few dB around it; with no speech (clips in mode bed or mute) it is mixed over the bed, which is not normalised (about -24 LUFS), with the effect lifted a few dB so that it peaks around -12 to -10 LUFS and cuts through a trend sound at -14. Without id it gets the next free "s<n>". Without variant the category's first variant is used; "auto" varies it by the item id. Move it with move_item (at_ms) and remove it with remove_sound.

id.title: Sound id
id.description: Optional id for the new effect. Without it the next free "s<n>" is used. It must not be in use anywhere in the timeline. The id also drives the effect's jitter and the "auto" variant.

at_ms.title: Start
at_ms.description: When the effect starts in the output, in ms.

gain_db.title: Gain
gain_db.description: Volume change in dB, -30 to +6. Default 0.
